title: Canary Orbit Playbook and Weekmap — Apr 2026
content:
Overview:
This is a working playbook for a short, controlled canary campaign we’re calling the ‘Canary Orbit’. The goal is to validate a small set of runtime changes that impact request batching and KV cache eviction heuristics (runtime PR 1543), observe real traffic behavior, and exercise rollback/mitigation lanes before a broader rollout. Keep this lean: 7-day observation window with incremental audience expansion across three orbit lanes.

Objectives:
- Verify p95 latency and tail-Q behavior under real user mixes after batching heuristics change.
- Detect regressions in per-tenant token cost and error modes (502/timeout).
- Validate health of automatic prefix cache warmup and eviction under mixed-seq workloads.
- Prove rollback path and communications for a <30 minute mitigation.

High-level schedule (Weekmap — Apr 12–18, 2026):
- Day -3 (Apr 9): Preflight dry-run in staging with synthetic mix, capture golden traces. (Owners: Riley / SRE)
- Day -1 (Apr 11): Pre-deploy checklist review + ops war room scheduling 09:00 PT. Confirm runbook pinned in Slack #release-ops.
- D0 (Apr 12) 07:00 PT: Canary lane A (internal traffic only) — 1% traffic, duration 3h.
- D0 (Apr 12) 11:00 PT: Evaluate signals; if green, expand to lane B.
- D0 (Apr 12) 13:00 PT: Canary lane B — 5% traffic, duration 6h.
- D1 (Apr 13) 09:00 PT: Day recap sync — quick retro and decision for lane C.
- D1 (Apr 13) 12:00 PT: Canary lane C — 20% traffic, duration 24h rolling windows.
- D2–D7 (Apr 14–18): Observability sweep, additional telemetry capture, and post-canary validation. Decision gate on Apr 18 10:00 PT for full rollout scheduling.

Preflight checklist (must be green before D0):
- [ ] Staging run with 90th/95th/99th latency traces attached to the run (file: staging-canary-golden-2026-04-09.trace).
- [ ] Canary deployment config reviewed (owner: Priya) — feature flags, percent targets, autoscale bounds.
- [ ] Rollback artifact built and smoke-tested (tag: rollback/v1543-quick).
- [ ] Alerts and dashboards validated: p95 latency, error rate, CPU/GPU saturation, token-per-request delta.
- [ ] Pager duty roster confirmed for 72 hours post-deploy.
- [ ] Stakeholders notified (CS, Solutions Eng, Product) with expected windows and channels.

Orbit lanes (audience segmentation):
- Lane A — Orbit 0: internal-only, non-production accounts, 1% of global traffic. Fast fail gate.
- Lane B — Orbit 1: small set of low-risk customers (opt-in canaries), 5% traffic. Prefer customers with automated retry logic.
- Lane C — Orbit 2: general production but limited to region/us-west-2 and <20% of traffic. Run longer observation windows here.

Observability signals & thresholds (siren-level thresholds):
- Green: p95 latency <= baseline + 15ms AND 5xx rate < 0.2% absolute increase over baseline.
- Yellow: p95 latency increase between +15ms and +40ms OR 5xx increase between 0.2% and 0.5% — require ops lead triage within 20 minutes.
- Red: p95 latency > baseline + 40ms OR 5xx increase > 0.5% OR sustained CPU/GPU saturation > 85% for 5m — immediate rollback and paging.
- Secondary signals: token cost delta > +7% (billing metric), memory OOM events, queue depth growth beyond 2x baseline.

Rollback criteria & quick steps:
- Criteria (any one triggers rollback):
  * Red siren condition.
  * User-reported functional failures affecting core flows (CS escalations > 3 incidents in 30m).
  * Telemetry inconsistency with warmup expectations (cache warmup fail rate > 10%).
- One-click rollback path:
  1) Set feature-flag runtime.batch.inflight = false (ops flagging path).
  2) Trigger rollback pipeline tag rollback/v1543-quick (CI job) to deploy previous runtime.
  3) Run smoke tests via /internal/smoke and confirm 200/healthy on 10 sample endpoints.
  4) Announce rollback in #release-ops and page on-call SRE.
  5) File incident stub and assign to on-call for postmortem.

Mitigation lanes before rollback (if Yellow):
- Narrow traffic: scale back to Lane A (internal) while investigating.
- Throttle batching aggressiveness via runtime tunable (owner: Ethan).
- Flip KV eviction to conservative mode (runtime.kv.eviction=conservative).

Communication plan:
- Ingress channel: #release-ops Slack. Use pinned template: "[CANARY] <lane> <status> <short summary> <action> <link to dashboard>".
- External-facing: customer-notify draft (for opt-in customers in Lane B) prepared by CS (Sofia). Only publish post-D0 if lane B shows prolonged issues.
- Exec summary: Day 0 end-of-day email to heads of Eng/Product with baseline comparisons + action items.

Release notes (draft — to be polished for broader rollout):
- Title: Runtime batching & KV eviction tuning (v1.1543)
- What: Adjustments to the batching heuristics to reduce per-token overhead and a safer default KV cache eviction policy.
- Why: To reduce tail latency for mixed-sequence workloads and lower per-request GPU time for short sequences.
- Risk/Impact: Small risk of transient latencies during warmup and increased token cost for a tiny subset of long-sequence customers. We will monitor and rollback if major regressions are observed.
- Rollout plan: Gradual canary across three orbit lanes (internal → opt-in customers → region-limited production) over 7 days.

Quick runbook: Day-of checklist (Ops lead copy)
- 06:30 PT: Check preflight checklist status.
- 06:50 PT: Warn on-call + send pre-deploy note to #release-ops.
- 07:00 PT: Deploy lane A. Watch p95/p99 and 5xx for first 30m.
- 07:45 PT: Quick sync message with owners. Decision: expand or rollback.

Data capture and artifacts (attach after run):
- Traces: run-2026-04-12-canaryA.trc, run-2026-04-12-canaryB.trc.
- Metrics snapshot: metrics-snapshot-2026-04-12-12z.csv.
- Perf diff notebook: perf-diff-v1543.ipynb

Open questions / action items:
- [ ] Confirm whether lane B customers should be explicitly opted-in or opt-out (Product to decide).
- [ ] Add token-cost alert as a first-class metric in Grafana (owner: Priya).
- [ ] Validate rollback automation from the on-call phone flow (test window Apr 10).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the escalation path short — we want to avoid chase-and-wait. If in doubt, tighten audience rather than risk broad exposure.
- This run should also exercise our telemetry retention pipeline; capture raw traces for 48h.

Appendix: Useful links
- Staging runbook: https://confluence.internal/redwood/staging-canary
- Runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1543
- Jira epic: https://jira.internal/browse/JIRA-3421

(End of draft — please add observations and edit the release notes section after D1 retrospective.)
